answer:
For high-risk pregnant patients, the use of baby aspirin (low-dose) starting at 12-28 weeks of gestation is recommended to reduce the risk of preeclampsia. This recommendation is provided in the ACOG Practice Bulletin on Preeclampsia [ACOG, 2020]. 

For other indications such as primary prevention of cardiovascular disease, aspirin is not typically prescribed according to the ACC/AHA Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease Guideline [ACC/AHA, 2019]. This guideline does not support routine use and recommends a personalized risk-benefit discussion with the clinician rather than aspirin initiation. 

Please ensure to discuss these recommendations specifically tailored for you or your patient with their healthcare provider due to individual variances.

results.content: Low-dose aspirin starting at 12-28 weeks of gestation is recommended for patients at high risk of preeclampsia. Magnesium sulfate is recommended for seizure prophylaxis in patients with severe features of preeclampsia.

Aspirin for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease is not routinely recommended due to bleeding risk, except in select high-risk adults 40-70 years after a risk-benefit discussion with their clinician.
results.source: ACC/AHA Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease Guideline
results.citation: Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease, ACC/AHA, 2019
